properties.decision:
RECORDED AS AN OPEN QUESTION, NOT SETTLED. Surfaced by running impact-check on chg:content-path-no-default AFTER the edit rather than before — the blast radius named ifc:mcp-tools as a boundary crossing, which is exactly the "changed one side of a contract" case that skill exists to catch. STILL OPEN.

WHAT THE FIX DID. Removing `default_value` from `--content-path` makes the refusal in `ReflowService::content_store` reachable, which is correct for the WRITE path and is what ver:content-surface already claims. But all four content tools route through that same method (content_tools.rs:97, :129, :155, :185), so `content_manifest` and `content_exists` now refuse too. Before the fix, `content_manifest` on an unconfigured server ANSWERED — `entries: []`, `total_bytes: 0`, `store_root: "./reflow2-content"` — and that answer was worse than useless, because the root it named did not exist. So the fix is not a regression; the question is whether refusing is the RIGHT answer or merely a less-wrong one.

THE CASE FOR REFUSING (what ships now): a manifest says "whether the bytes are here", and with no store there is no "here". `req:no-silent-fallback` argues the same way for reads as for writes, and the refusal names the remedy.

THE CASE FOR ANSWERING, and it is not weak: cap:content-manifest exists for the person "handed the design ON ITS OWN", and its whole point is that `missing` names content the graph references and this checkout does not have — "so a diagram that will not open is a named finding rather than a silent absence". That reader has NO store by definition. Refusing tells them to configure one before they can be told what they are missing, which inverts the capability. The honest answer for them is every referenced hash listed under `missing`, `orphaned: []`, and the store named as absent. `content_exists` has the same shape: it is documented as the cheap "do I have everything?" call.

WHY IT IS MOOT TODAY AND WILL NOT STAY MOOT: reflow2's own graph references ZERO content (136 Fragments, 0 with a `content_ref`), so both behaviours return the same information here. The distinction only bites once a design actually points at bytes — which is exactly when the person who needs it is the one who cannot answer it. Deciding it now costs nothing; discovering it then costs a user.

BEARS ON req:the-store-is-reachable-from-a-session, which sits in the direct ring of this change. Whether "reachable" means "the tools are present and say what is wrong" or "the store exists without anyone choosing where" is the requirement's own ambiguity, and it should be read before this is settled rather than after.
properties.name: ACCEPTED 2026-08-06 — content_manifest and content_exists ANSWER when no store is configured; only content_put and content_get refuse
properties.rationale:
Resolved by Anthony 2026-08-06, taking the ANSWER branch: the reader cap:content-manifest exists for is "someone handed the design ON ITS OWN", and that reader has no store by definition, so refusing them inverts the capability. Surfaced only because impact-check was run on chg:content-path-no-default and named ifc:mcp-tools as a boundary crossing — without it the refusal would have shipped on all four tools unnoticed, which is the value of that skill stated concretely rather than in principle.

WHAT SHIPPED: DesignGraph::content_manifest now takes Option<&ContentStore>. With None, every referenced hash reports missing, orphaned is empty (no bytes exist to be unreferenced), total_bytes is 0, and store_root says "(no content store configured)" in words instead of naming a directory nobody chose. ReflowService::content_store_for_reading returns Option and is used by the two read tools; content_store (the refusing form) still backs content_put and content_get unchanged.

WHY THE SPLIT IS PRINCIPLED RATHER THAN A COMPROMISE: req:no-silent-fallback forbids INVENTING a location, and neither path does that any more — the write refuses and names the remedy, the read reports absence as absence. The old behaviour violated it in the worst way, answering with a store_root of "./reflow2-content" for a directory that existed nowhere. Both halves now say something true.

PROVEN, not asserted: crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/tools.rs the_manifest_answers_without_a_store_while_writes_still_refuse holds all three behaviours in one case, deliberately beside a_server_with_no_content_store_says_so_instead_of_choosing_one so the pair reads as the contract. 70/70 tools tests and 15/15 core content tests pass; clippy -D warnings clean across both crates.
